title: Flow Matching from Viewpoint of Proximal Operators
claim: Optimal transport couples each noise point to a manifold point along the normal direction, so the data manifold is geometrically stable.
layout: 1 square plot, centered circle with colored radial rays, labeled angles
description: A single 2-D scatter-style plot with axes x_0^(1) and x_0^(2) running from -3 to 3. A blue unit circle, the data manifold, sits at the center. Faint concentric lavender circles show the Gaussian source density. Five colored dots sit on the circle at labeled angles θ=0, π/4, π/2, π and 1.5π. Each dot has a same-colored half line or ray: orange runs right, red left, purple up, yellow down, and green diagonal. These rays start near the left of the circle, around x≈-0.8, and extend outward to the plot edge. Small x markers show where the rays start. The eye goes first to the bright rays crossing the circle, then to the labeled dots. The rays show which source points are coupled to which manifold points.
caption: Examples of coupling. $P_0=N(0,I_2)$ and $P_1$: von Mises distribution $\rho_{1,0}$. The point on the circle and the half line in the same color are coupled by OT. Note that the direction of $\partial\phi(x_1)$ is normal to the manifold at $x_1$.
abstract: We discuss the dynamics of Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM) under the manifold hypothesis, where the support of the target distribution is a low dimensional manifold. We first derive an exact proximal expression of the vector field, using an extended Brenier potential for the OT; the vector field can be expressed by a denoiser, which is presented as the proximal operator associated with the potential function. Based on this explicit proximal form of the vector field, we analyze the manifold stability for perturbations to initial points, using the Lyapunov exponents of the dynamics. By analyzing the local behavior with the tools in convex analysis, we show that the dynamics contract linearly in the perturbation of the normal directions to the manifold, while perturbations in the tangential directions are preserved; this implies the stability of the manifold structure to the perturbations. To justify the theoretical arguments on the population OT, we also establish the convergence of minibatch OT-CFM with neural network learning to population OT-CFM under regularity and stability assumptions, with rate exponents governed by the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold. Experiments on synthetic data, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 support the predicted geometric behavior.
